target_customer: Developers and companies that need managed, hosted databases (originally MongoDB, later Elasticsearch, Redis, PostgreSQL, RethinkDB)
problem: Running, scaling and securing a database yourself is operational work; MongoHQ/Compose hosted and managed it for a monthly fee.
business_model: Usage/plan-based subscription for managed database hosting, also sold through PaaS add-on marketplaces (Heroku, CloudBees)

founders.name: Jason McCay
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch 2011 and CloudBees post; bio not found.

founders.name: Ben Wyrosdick
founders.background_notes: Company release says MongoHQ was founded by Wyrosdick and McCay in 2009.

founders.name: Kurt Mackey
founders.background_notes: Quoted as co-founder and CEO at the 2014 rename and 2015 IBM deal; not named in 2011 coverage.

technical_complexity.rationale: Operating replica-set MongoDB reliably for many tenants was standard but demanding infrastructure engineering; no research-grade problem. Rating is my judgment from product description.

defensibility.rationale: Hosted databases are copyable and dependent on the underlying open-source engine and cloud hosts; some stickiness once data lives there.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: In 2015 IBM bought the company rather than copying it (Cloud Data Services group, Bluemix). Later cloud providers shipped managed MongoDB; not researched in detail.

market_need_then: Hosted MongoDB was already being asked for in 2009 (AVC post), and by 2011 PaaS platforms (Heroku, CloudBees) integrated MongoHQ as an add-on; in 2012 the company reported being profitable with about 20% month-over-month growth for the prior year (company statement via TechCrunch).

branding.name_origin: MongoHQ: hosted-MongoDB headquarters, derived from the MongoDB product name (inferred by name only; no source on intent). Compose (Aug 2014): CEO Kurt Mackey tied it to the computing idea of composition, combining existing functions into new ones, as the company moved beyond MongoDB.
branding.domain_note: Compose used compose.io after the Aug 2014 rename; MongoHQ domain mongohq.com remained the directory website.

rebrands.why: Expansion beyond MongoDB (Elasticsearch launched at the same time); name tied to MongoDB was limiting

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage shows a functional developer-tool brand known through add-on marketplaces; no sourced evidence of mascot, community or merch. Rating is a weak judgment.

pivots.to: Multi-database platform (Compose: Elasticsearch, Redis, PostgreSQL, others)

outcome_analysis: Compose (MongoHQ) rode the growth of MongoDB and PaaS platforms, distributing through Heroku and CloudBees add-ons, reported profitability and 20% monthly growth in 2012, raised about 6.4M in total, broadened into a multi-database platform in 2014 and was acquired by IBM in July 2015 with undisclosed terms and about 3,600 customers. It is a modest but real exit; the price is not public.
notes: Founding year: company release says 2009, YC batch S11 (the directory-era depth-1 said 2011). Search snippets only; I did not fetch the pages (company website and YC page not fetched). Funding totals: 417K + 6M matches the 6.4M total in 2015 coverage, so coverage is likely near complete but marked partial. The 2011 MongoLab competitor entry has no traction data; MongoLab was cited only in the TechCrunch snippet. Founder backgrounds not found. Acquisition price undisclosed.
